name: CloudCannon
title: Mica vs. CloudCannon
summary: CloudCannon is a hosted service with visual on-page editing, roles, deploy previews and support. Mica is free, runs on your own machine or server, and has an MCP server for AI agents.

chooseMica.text: You want AI agents to edit your content: Mica has an MCP server built in. CloudCannon has agent skills, a CLI and an API, but no MCP server.

Your entries link to data that lives elsewhere: product data, place names, regions or codes. Mica has typed relations to thousands of items from a JSON or CSV file of your website, and never edits them. CloudCannon feeds select inputs from data files, but has no typed relation field.
You want open source under the MIT licence, with no vendor service and no per-user price.
You want to run the editor yourself, behind any OpenID Connect provider.
You need a map to pick places, and the page should show the same view: Mica stores the zoom with the place.

chooseOther.text: Editors should edit on the page itself, with visual editing.
You want a hosted service with support.
Your editors need roles, with permission groups.
You want deploy previews of pull requests (Team plan and up).
Editors should publish a branch with a pull request for approval.
You want to keep media in a DAM, such as S3, Cloudinary or Bynder.
